title: BCA/7/2024 of STATE OF UTTARAKHAND Vs SURENDRA SINGH

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Bail Cancellation Application No. 07 of 2024
State of Uttarakhand ........Applicant

Present:-
Mr. Virendra Singh Rawat, AGA with Ms. Rangoli Purohit,
Advocate for the applicant.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 The respondent was granted bail by the court
of Special Sessions Judge, Champawat in Bail Application
No.94 of 2023, Surendra Singh vs. State in FIR No.67 of
2023, under Sections 8/20 of the Narcotic Drugs and
Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 ("the Act"), Police
Station Kotwali Champawat, District Champawat on
10.11.2023. The State has challenged the bail order by
way of filing the instant bail cancellation application.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. According to the FIR, on 27.10.2023, at about
10:29 AM, a Sub Inspector, Police Station Champawat
had received a call from a Constable that he had detected

2
a bag containing Charas in a roadways bus. Based on this
information, at 11:01 AM, Sub Inspector proceeded to the
spot and found a bag in the isles of the bus. A search was
made, but no person claimed ownership over the bag. The
bag was when minutely searched, according to the FIR,
an Aadhar Card was found in it and the photograph in
the Aadhar Card did match with the applicant, who was
sitting on a rear seat. The FIR records that the bus
conductor, driver and other passengers declined to be the
witness of the recovery because they could be late for
their assignments.
4. Learned counsel for the State would submit
that during investigation, the driver and conductor of the
bus have supported the prosecution case.
5. The Criminal Justice System of this country
favours individual liberty. Bail is a Rule and Jail is an
exception. There are various factors which governs grant
of bail. Cancellation of bail by a higher Court requires
consideration of various factors. An order granting bail
may not be easily disturbed. Freedom, as allowed may not
be curtailed on mere assertions.

3
6. The Sessions Court at para 11 has given
reasons for granting bail. The court found that after
leaving the Police Station at 11:01 AM by the Sub
Inspector, he would have reached at the spot within one
hour because its distance is 12 to 13 Kms. The
proceedings continued till 04:25 PM. Under such
circumstances, it cannot be believed that the independent
witnesses declined to be witnessed of the recovery on the
ground of delay. The court had observed that there were
Govt. officials in the bus including bus driver and bus
conductor. If they would have denied, the police would
have proceeded against them. The court also doubted the
presence of purse in an abandoned bag on the ground
that generally, no person keeps a purse in a bag.
7. It is a case of recovery of commercial quantity
of narcotic substance and in such cases Section 37 of
the Act makes specific provisions. Bail in such cases
may not be granted, unless the Court is satisfied that
there are reasonable grounds for believing that the
accused is not guilty of such offence and that he is not
likely to commit any offence while on bail.
8. The discussion that has been made by the
court in the impugned order dated 10.11.2023 at para 11,

4
as per court has been made in view of Section 37 of the
Act.
9. At the stage of considering the bail application,
the court is not required to go in the deeper scrutiny of
the matter. If discussion in the light of Section 37 of the
Act is made in the order granting bail, in the cases of
recovery of commercial quantity merely because the exact
wording of the provision of Section 37 is not written, it
may not effect the bail order.
10. There may be multiple questions that would be
asked during trial, apart from assumption that generally
no person keeps his purse or identity card/proof in a bag
containing Charas, which is in an abandoned condition in
the isles of the bus, the question that may arise is, as to
how the photograph was identified? Have all the
passengers lined up? Who has identified? When the
Aadhar Card of the accused was made? These and many
more questions would find scrutiny during trial.
11. Having considered the factual narration and
the analysis that had been made in the impugned bail
order dated 10.11.2023, this Court is of the view that no
interference is warranted in the bail order. Accordingly,

5
instant bail cancellation application deserves to be
dismissed at the stage of admission itself.
12. The bail cancellation application is dismissed in
limine.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 08.04.2024
Sanjay
